log._case: at overflows Double -> Number('1e400') is Infinity, clamp to 0

IEEE-754 witness (2^53 + 1): 9007199254740993 is a VALID Kotlin Long but is NOT representable as a binary64 double. Both the oracle (Number()) and Kotlin (String.toDouble()) parse to the NEAREST double 9007199254740992 = 2^53, which rounds DOWN by 1. An exact-integer parser (BigDecimal/BigInteger) would keep ...993 and diverge from Desktop; the contract is nearest-double rounding, then trunc.
log.text: at is 2^53 + 1, first integer a double cannot represent

log._case: IEEE-754 witness (2^53 + 3): 9007199254740995 is a valid Long whose nearest double is 9007199254740996, ONE ABOVE it — double parsing can round UP as well as down. Desktop's Number() and Kotlin's toDouble() agree on this; the value stored is the double, not the input integer.
log.text: at is 2^53 + 3, nearest double rounds up

log._case: IEEE-754 witness (2^62 + 1): mid-range probe. 4611686018427387905 is odd and above 2^53; doubles this large are spaced 1024 apart, so the nearest double is 4611686018427387904 = 2^62, off by 1. Any parser that claims exact Long round-trip through a double silently changes the watermark basis here.

IEEE-754 witness (largest double below 2^63, minus 1): 9223372036854774785 is a valid Long one above the largest representable double 9223372036854774784 (2^63 - 2^10). It parses DOWN to ...784 and stays a legitimate Long-storable timestamp — accepted (not clamped), because the contract is nearest-double rounding, not integer exactness.
log.text: at is one above the largest Long-storable double

log._case: at is finite but exceeds Kotlin Long storage -> mobile clamps to 0. NOTE: the Desktop-domain normAt KEEPS this value (it is a finite double); only normAtMobileLong rejects it. EXPECTED.json carries both columns, and _expect_at follows the MOBILE column.

LONG BOUNDARY: 2^63 = 9223372036854775808 is the double nearest Long.MAX_VALUE and sits one ABOVE it. A guard written as '> Number(Long.MAX_VALUE)' compares against this same 2^63 and lets it through, where Kotlin Double.toLong() saturates to Long.MAX_VALUE -- permanently poisoning the monotonic read watermark. Correct cut is >= 2^63.
LONG BOUNDARY: Long.MAX_VALUE itself (9223372036854775807) is NOT representable as a double -- it rounds UP to 2^63, so it must be rejected too. This is the probe that fails against a '>' guard.
log.text: at is Long.MAX_VALUE as a string

log._case: LONG BOUNDARY: 9223372036854774784 is the LARGEST double below 2^63 and is exactly representable as a Long. It must pass through unchanged -- a guard that over-rejects would zero a legitimate timestamp. No double exists between this value and 2^63.
log.text: at is the largest representable Long-storable double
